title: Low-nonlinearity advantage of hollow-core fiber for wavelength multiplexing of quantum entanglement and classical DWDM signals
abstract: Coexistence of classical and quantum light in optical fiber is a key requirement for scalable quantum networks. However, it is fundamentally limited by nonlinear crosstalk from intense classical signals. Hollow-core fiber (HCF), with its intrinsically low optical nonlinearity, offers a promising solution. Here, we experimentally demonstrate the coexistence of polarization-entangled photons with dense wavelength-division multiplexed (DWDM) classical signals with a total launch power of 11.2 dBm, and perform a direct comparison between equal-length single-mode fiber (SMF) and photonic-bandgap-based HCF deployed in a campus network. We observe that HCF suppresses background noise by approximately two orders of magnitude compared to SMF, while preserving high-fidelity entanglement distribution. Our results provide clear experimental evidence of the advantage of HCF and establish its potential as a transmission medium.

title: Fate of Discrete Time Crystals in Finite-Size Cavity QED Systems
abstract: It has been shown that Discrete Time Crystal (DTC) behavior may arise in the periodically driven, open Dicke model in the thermodynamic limit ($N \rightarrow \infty$). In this work, we demonstrate that finite $N$ non-mean-field fluctuations in this model can lead to decay rates and amplitudes of transient DTCs that display a non-trivial non-monotonic behavior with an increasing number of atoms. We show that the second-order cumulant expansion fails to capture the finite-size dynamics, while a stochastic version of the Truncated Wigner Approximation (TWA) is remarkably accurate, particularly in the large atom ensemble limit. Using the TWA and the Monte Carlo Wave Function (MCWF) approach, we identify three distinct dynamical regimes of transient DTC behavior in the finite-size Dicke model. We outline the mechanism behind the non-monotonic finite size dynamical decay of DTC order and discuss the implications for experiments performed on finite-sized atomic assemblies.
subjects: Quantum Physics (quant-ph) ; Quantum Gases (cond-mat.quant-gas); Atomic Physics (physics.atom-ph)

summaries.en: Finite-size non-mean-field fluctuations in the periodically driven open Dicke model produce transient discrete time crystal decay rates and amplitudes that vary non-monotonically with atom number, with a stochastic Truncated Wigner Approximation capturing the dynamics accurately and revealing three distinct dynamical regimes.

title: Resolving Nonlocal State Reduction via Induced Coherence in Frequency-Comb Biphoton Sources
abstract: How macroscopic definite outcomes and nonlocal correlations emerge from entangled superpositions across spacelike-separated regions without superluminal action or {\it ad hoc} wavefunction collapse remains a defining open question in the foundations of quantum mechanics. Here, we resolve this century-long paradox within \textit{linear} relativistic quantum electrodynamics by developing an open-system and measurement-defined framework realized in dual, spacelike-separated nonlinear crystals driven synchronously by a multi-mode optical frequency comb and seeded by an ultra-narrow coherent laser. Expanding the transverse electromagnetic vector potential into discrete single-photon frequency-comb supermodes, we show that tracing out the unmeasured continuous-wave idler field yields an exact spatial dephasing Lindblad master equation whose decoherence rate is governed by the non-orthogonal state overlap of single-photon-added coherent states. Connecting this open-system map to free-vector-space quotient measurement theory, we demonstrate that single-particle interference arises from the geometric projection of the composite state onto detector-defined conditional cosets rather than remote collapse, establishing strict operational equivalence across pump, seed, and signal phase scans. The resulting wave-particle-entanglement triality equality $P^2 + E^2 + V^2 = 1$ is saturated across the complete parameter space, while the atomic-clock-referenced comb structure anchors continuous-variable time-frequency displacement stabilizers directly at the hardware layer. Our work unifies induced coherence, Bohr's complementarity, and quotient measurement theory, providing a microscopic pathway toward fault-tolerant bosonic quantum information processing.

summaries.en: By tracing out the idler field in a frequency-comb biphoton source, the authors derive an exact spatial dephasing Lindblad master equation and show, within linear relativistic quantum electrodynamics, that single-particle interference arises from geometric projection of the composite state onto detector-defined conditional cosets rather than nonlocal collapse, saturating the wave-particle-entanglement triality equality P^2 + E^2 + V^2 = 1.

title: Single-photon time qubit: Quantum-vacuum control and complementarity of the arrow of time
abstract: Treating the arrow of time as a controllable quantum variable rather than a fixed external parameter is a central challenge in quantum physics. Recently, Bloch~\cite{Bloch2025} proposed the theoretical concept of a \emph{time qubit}, a two-level control space $\mathcal{H}_T=\mathrm{span}\{\ket{+},\ket{-}\}$ that selects between opposite Hamiltonian evolutions $\hat{H}_{\pm}=\hat{H}_0\pm\hat{V}$, but this paradigm has remained experimentally unrealized. Here we formulate the quantum-optical theory of a single-photon time qubit---uncovering quantum-vacuum control and complementarity of the arrow of time---and experimentally probe and validate its predictions using phase-resolved single-photon interferometry from two coherently seeded entangled nonlinear biphoton sources~\cite{Lee2018,Yoon2021}. First, we show theoretically and verify experimentally that a controlled $\pi$ pump--seed phase inversion during pair creation from the quantum vacuum flips the stimulated displacement generator $\hat{V}\to -\hat{V}$ on top of the spontaneous two-mode squeezing background $\hat{H}_0$, reversing the stimulated evolution time [$\hat{U}_{\mathrm{stim},-}(t)=\hat{U}_{\mathrm{stim},+}(-t)$] and enabling universal single-qubit $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ control and postselection-free first-order tomography on the temporal Bloch sphere. Second, we prove that spontaneous idler vacuum fluctuations record complete which-branch (temporal-direction) information whereas the shared coherent seed erases it without cascading or aligning the idler beams, establishing an exact wave--particle complementarity law $|\bm{r}|=\mathcal{V}=|\alpha|^2/(1+|\alpha|^2)$ for the purity of the arrow of time and enabling direct first-order measurement of the Loschmidt time-reversal echo.

summaries.en: The paper presents the theory and experimental validation of a single-photon time qubit, showing that a controlled pump–seed phase inversion flips the stimulated displacement generator to reverse the stimulated evolution time and enables SU(2) control on the temporal Bloch sphere, while spontaneous idler vacuum fluctuations record which-branch information that the coherent seed erases, yielding an exact complementarity law between arrow-of-time purity and visibility.

title: Multimode Parametric Amplifier for K-Band Quantum Measurements
abstract: We demonstrate K-band nondegenerate three-wave-mixing amplification in a multimode resonator comprising an array of 500 SNAILs. Pairing K-band signal modes with lower-frequency internal idler modes enables 20 dB of gain continuously from 19.6 to 25.6 GHz with pump frequencies below 32.2 GHz. At 20 dB gain, the 3-dB bandwidth ranges from 2.6 to 11.7 MHz, and the input-referred 1-dB compression power reaches -100.9 dBm. In the 20-22 GHz band, the average added noise is 0.73 quanta. A two-mode nondegenerate parametric amplification model describes the measured gain response and gain-bandwidth behavior, while a multimode Kerr model captures the overall compression scale. Our amplifier provides a practical solution for implementing a state-of-the-art readout of superconducting qubits in the K-band.

title: Narrowband nonreciprocal transmission in a Doppler-broadened multilevel atomic system
abstract: We theoretically investigate narrowband nonreciprocal transmission in a Doppler-broadened five-level M-type atomic medium. After Doppler averaging, the M-type system retains a narrow near-resonant electromagnetically induced transparency window that is narrower than that of a standard three-level $\Lambda$ system. This spectral narrowing is associated with the decreasing separation between the two inner dressed states as atomic velocity increases. The transparency window exhibits pronounced direction-dependent transmission, with high forward transmission and strong suppression in the reverse direction. The transparency linewidth and forward-backward probe transmission can be controlled via two independent driving fields, while the central transparency frequency is kept essentially unchanged. The resulting narrowband nonreciprocity supports high forward transmission together with strong suppression in the reverse direction, which is suitable for frequency-selective optical filtering and nonreciprocal optical transmission in thermal atomic media. Our scheme with these specific features is geared towards enabling compact vapor-cell-based nonreciprocal devices for quantum network applications.

summaries.en: This theoretical study demonstrates narrowband nonreciprocal transmission in a Doppler-broadened five-level M-type atomic medium, where a narrow velocity-dependent EIT window enables high forward transmission and strong reverse-direction suppression controllable via two driving fields, suitable for frequency-selective filtering and compact vapor-cell nonreciprocal devices in quantum networks.
summaries.zh: 该理论研究展示了多普勒展宽的五级M型原子介质中的窄带非互易传输，其中随速度变化而变窄的电磁诱导透明窗口可实现高正向透射和强烈的反向抑制，并可通过两个独立驱动场调控，适用于频率选择滤波及量子网络中的紧凑型蒸气池非互易器件。
summaries.ja: 本研究はドップラー広がりを持つ5準位M型原子媒質における狭帯域非相反透過を理論的に示し、原子速度に依存して狭くなる電磁誘起透明窓により高い前方透過と強い逆方向抑制が得られ、2つの独立した駆動場で制御可能で、周波数選択フィルタや量子ネットワーク向けの小型蒸気セル非相反デバイスに適することを明らかにした。

title: Trapped-ion-based quantum repeater node across a 17 km metropolitan fiber
abstract: Concatenation of quantum repeater nodes has been proposed as a means to distribute entanglement efficiently across future long-distance networks. Here, we demonstrate a trapped-ion repeater node that establishes photonic entanglement over a 17 km fiber traversing a city, moving beyond laboratory-only prototypes. The node comprises two atomic ions coupled to an optical cavity. First, a detailed characterization is performed of the long fiber channel and of ion-photon entanglement distributed across it. Next, a repeater-node protocol is implemented, achieving entanglement between a local photon and a remote photon with a Bell-state fidelity of $81.6^{+1.9}_{-1.4}\%$. These results demonstrate that trapped-ion repeater-node technology can operate over existing city-scale fiber infrastructure and represent a step toward distributed quantum repeater networks.

summaries.en: A trapped-ion quantum repeater node established photonic entanglement over a 17 km metropolitan fiber, achieving a Bell-state fidelity of 81.
summaries.zh: 一个囚禁离子量子中继节点通过横跨城市的17公里光纤建立光子纠缠，在本地光子与远程光子之间实现了81.
summaries.ja: 都市を横断する17kmの光ファイバー上で捕捉イオンの量子リピーターノードが光子もつれを確立し、局所光子と遠隔光子の間で81.

title: Phase shifts and fluctuations from motional, relativistic, and dark-matter effects in ion-trap clocks
abstract: Ions possess both center-of-mass motion and internal states, rendering trapped-ion optical clocks susceptible to perturbations of both degrees of freedom, which results in systematic shifts and fluctuations with motional and relativistic origins. We develop a quantum theory that connects these effects to filter functions determined by the employed pulse sequences and show how the interrogation can be tailored to suppress or enhance specific perturbations. Our treatment includes laser frequency noise and motional effects such as recoil and Doppler shifts, micromotion and excess micromotion, as well as state-dependent trap imperfections and accelerations, e.g., caused by Stark shifts. We further account for relativistic effects including time dilation and the mass defect, and show how the same framework can be applied to hypothetical dark-matter signals. By considering ensemble-averaged phases and their variances, we characterize both systematic shifts and fluctuations, while asynchronous operation relative to the Paul-trap drive allows motional fluctuations to average down between runs. Our results provide a unified framework for characterizing and controlling the systematic and statistical contributions that determine the trueness and precision of trapped-ion optical clocks.
subjects: Quantum Physics (quant-ph) ; Atomic and Molecular Clusters (physics.atm-clus)

summaries.en: The paper develops a unified quantum theory connecting motional, relativistic, and dark-matter perturbations in trapped-ion optical clocks to filter functions set by the interrogation pulse sequence, enabling systematic shifts and fluctuations to be characterized and controlled through tailored interrogation.
summaries.zh: 该论文建立了一个统一的量子理论，将离子阱光钟中的运动、相对论和暗物质扰动与被询问脉冲序列决定的滤波函数联系起来，从而能够通过定制询问来表征和控制系统性频移与涨落。
summaries.ja: 本論文は、イオントラップ光時計における運動・相対論・暗黒物質由来の摂動を、質問パルス系列で決まるフィルタ関数に結び付ける統一的な量子理論を構築し、質問の設計により系統的シフトと揺らぎを特性評価・制御できることを示す。

title: CO$Φ$ - COmpiling PHotonics into dIgital quantum circuits
abstract: Photonic and qubit-based (digital) approaches to quantum computing are largely regarded as separate paradigms. This article aims to bridge these paradigms by developing a method for mapping quantum-optical systems onto qubit-based quantum circuits. The key ingredient enabling this mapping is the introduction of a truncation of the Fock space describing single-mode optical states. Within this framework, representations of basic photonic operations are developed, including the phase-rotation operator, the displacement operator, the squeezing operator, and the beam splitter. Explicit quantum circuit constructions are provided for Fock-space truncations of dimension $N=2$ and $N=4$. We discuss benchmarking of the implemented operations and identify the regime of applicability and the limitations of the proposed method. The presented results can be used to simulate quantum optical circuits on qubit-based quantum computers, with special relevance to Gaussian Boson Sampling in the low-photon-number regime. To demonstrate the practical applicability of this approach, we complement the theoretical framework with a Python-based quantum programming tool CO$\Phi$ that compiles Blackbird quantum-optics programs into qubit-based OpenQASM circuits using a truncated Fock-space encoding. The compiler is available on GitHub at this https URL .

summaries.en: The paper introduces COΦ, a method and Python compiler that maps photonic quantum-optics circuits onto qubit-based digital quantum circuits by truncating the Fock space to dimensions N=2 and N=4 and representing basic operations such as phase rotation, displacement, squeezing, and beam splitting as explicit quantum circuits, with relevance to low-photon-number Gaussian Boson Sampling.
summaries.zh: 该论文提出了COΦ方法与Python编译器，通过将Fock空间截断到N=2和N=4维度并把相位旋转、位移、压缩和分束等基本操作表示为显式量子电路，从而将光子量子光学线路映射到基于量子比特的数字量子电路，适用于低光子数区域的高斯玻色采样。
summaries.ja: 本論文はCOΦと呼ぶ手法とPythonコンパイラを提案し、フォック空間をN=2およびN=4に打ち切ることで位相回転・変位・スクイージング・ビームスプリッターなどの基本操作を明示的な量子回路として表現し、光子量子光学回路を量子ビットベースのデジタル量子回路へ写像することを可能にし、低光子数領域のガウスボソンサンプリングに有用である。

title: Stable charged energy and phase transitions in an anisotropic Dicke quantum battery with Kerr nonlinearity
abstract: Phase transitions (PTs) in quantum many-body systems offer a powerful route to manipulate the performance of quantum batteries (QBs). Here, we investigate an anisotropic Dicke QB with Kerr nonlinearity, focusing on the role of PTs in the charging process of the QB system. By analyzing how the Kerr nonlinearity reshapes the cavity level-spacing structure, we find that multiple near-degeneracies emerge at specific nonlinearity strengths. Away from the region of multiple near-degeneracies, the stable stored energy is governed primarily by the ergodic-nonergodic transition (ENET), whereas within this region it is controlled by first- and second-order dissipative phase transitions (DPTs). We employ Liouvillian spectral theory to quantify the critical slowing down associated with the DPTs, and use the Wigner function to characterize the properties of the cavity field in the vicinity of criticality. We optimize the charging process via reinforcement learning (RL) and reveal the physical mechanism underlying performance enhancement from the perspective of ergodic and nonergodic phase dynamics. Our results offer a feasible pathway for manipulating and optimizing quantum battery performance based on intrinsic PT behaviors.

summaries.en: This study shows that in an anisotropic Dicke quantum battery with Kerr nonlinearity, stable stored energy is governed by the ergodic-nonergodic transition outside regions of multiple near-degeneracies but by first- and second-order dissipative phase transitions within them, with reinforcement learning optimizing charging via ergodic and nonergodic phase dynamics.
summaries.zh: 本研究表明，在具有克尔非线性的各向异性Dicke量子电池中，稳定储能远离多重近简并区时主要由遍历-非遍历转变决定，而在该区域内则由一阶和二阶耗散相变控制，并利用强化学习通过遍历与非遍历相动力学优化充电过程。
summaries.ja: 本研究は、カー非線形性を持つ異方的ディッケ量子電池において、安定な蓄エネルギーが多重近縮退領域の外ではエルゴード・非エルゴード転移に、その領域内では一次および二次の散逸相転移に支配されることを示し、強化学習によりエルゴード相・非エルゴード相のダイナミクスの観点から充電過程を最適化した。

title: Tuning between collective dynamics and scrambling through initial-state symmetry alignment in long-range spin models
abstract: Long-range interactions in many-body quantum systems give rise to a wide range of dynamical phenomena, from collective dynamics well described by integrable mean-field models with symmetric all-to-all couplings, to fast scrambling of quantum information from disordered long-range interactions. Here, we investigate scenarios in which both regimes emerge within a single deterministic, translation-invariant XY spin model with long-range couplings. We consider a sparse powers-of-two (PWR2) graph, where each spin interacts with a logarithmic number of neighbors, and a power-law-decaying model. By altering the initial state via local perturbations on a completely symmetric state, we show that the dynamics changes from collective to scrambling as witnessed by bipartite and multipartite entanglement measures. We characterize this collective-to-scrambling crossover using Lyapunov exponents in the semiclassical regime, and show that the spectral properties of the coupling graph adjacency matrix provide a very efficient tool to predict the onset of fast scrambling. Our results offer a unified framework for controlling the switch between collective and scrambling dynamics in a setup accessible in experiments with neutral atoms in cavities or in tweezer arrays.

summaries.en: By locally perturbing a fully symmetric initial state in deterministic, translation-invariant long-range XY spin models, the authors show that the dynamics can be tuned from collective mean-field behavior to fast scrambling, with the coupling graph's adjacency-matrix spectral properties efficiently predicting the onset of scrambling.
summaries.zh: 通过在确定性、平移不变的长程XY自旋模型中对完全对称的初始态施加局域扰动，作者表明动力学可以从集体平均场行为调控到快速扰乱，并且耦合图邻接矩阵的谱性质能够高效预测扰乱的 onset。
summaries.ja: 決定論的で並進不変な長距離XYスピンモデルにおいて、完全対称な初期状態に局所的摂動を加えることで、ダイナミクスを集団的平均場的振る舞いから高速スクランブリングへと調整でき、結合グラフの隣接行列のスペクトル特性がスクランブリングの開始を効率的に予測できることを示した。

title: Efficient Ground-State Manifold Amplification for Rydberg Atom Arrays via Houdayer Cluster Updates
abstract: We demonstrate a hybrid quantum-classical approach for exploring ground-state manifolds of maximum independent set problems, in which quantum hardware supplies the initial solutions and an entirely classical post-processing algorithm expands them, increasing the solution diversity of quantum hardware measurements by up to several orders of magnitude. Quantum optimization devices, while capable of generating high-quality solutions, can suffer from fundamental sampling limitations. This is particularly problematic for applications that strongly depend on a large variety of uncorrelated optimal solutions. We apply the Houdayer cluster update algorithm to systematically expand quantum-generated solution sets through classical post-processing. We validate our approach on a test bed of 43 problem instances from QuEra's Aquila analog annealing device, achieving diversity amplification factors, defined as the increase in the number of distinct solutions at a given set size, of up to 11923x with a median of 24.3x across different problem scales and hardness parameters. Because exact ground-state degeneracies are known for these instances, the recovered fraction of the manifold can be measured rather than bounded: post-processing recovers a median of 21% of the ground-state manifold, and provably all of it for six instances. We also demonstrate that, in some cases, the classical post-processing can discover independent sets larger than those found by the quantum hardware, thus improving on solution quality and not just diversity. While the method is non-ergodic and cannot guarantee complete manifold coverage, it consistently discovers a larger number of high-quality, and in some cases strictly better, configurations than quantum sampling alone. This work demonstrates how simple classical post-processing can enhance the utility of quantum optimization results.

title: NeST: ultra-high-rate qLDPC codes with sub-$50μ$s stabiliser cycles via spin shuttling
abstract: Quantum low-density parity-check codes now reach encoding rates up to 50% at useful distances. Their checks however are long-range group actions, not local neighbourhoods, and that connectivity has so far been supplied by neutral atoms. Silicon spin qubits offer the same primitive --- coherent transport of qubit blocks --- through electron shuttling, and on microsecond rather than millisecond timescales. They however travel along fabricated tracks rather than free space: permutations an atom array obtains by moving tweezers must here become collision-free motions on a physical lattice. We here present the first code and spin-qubit hardware co-design. We build an architecture whose geometry mimics that of a family of non-abelian groups, broad enough to host codes of excellent parameters: a hierarchy of nested conveyor-belt loops on a plain square lattice of shuttling tracks, in which every group multiplication becomes a rigid, globally controlled motion of whole qubit trains. We call it NeST, for Nested Shuttling Tracks. A code search over the family returns rate-20% mitten codes up to $[[1400,280,\leq 28]]$, and circuit-level simulations including shuttling dephasing give thresholds above $10^{-3}$ with sub-$50\mu$s stabiliser cycles, two to three orders of magnitude faster than neutral-atom implementations. Via extrapolations, we estimate that this largest code may reach a logical error probability per qubit per round of $10^{-14}$, assuming a ten-fold improvement on early shuttling demonstrations, with other physical errors at p=0.1%. Logic is compatible with NeST too: for the [[150,30,10]] code we build a code-surgery gadget in which every qubit again moves only by rigid belt motions, at no qubit cost and a 29% increase in gate layers. This demonstrates that ultra-low-overhead fault tolerance and a fast clock speed are not competing goals, and that silicon spin qubits can supply both.

summaries.en: The authors present NeST, a silicon spin-qubit architecture using nested conveyor-belt shuttling tracks on a square lattice that realizes non-abelian-group-based quantum LDPC codes, achieving rate-20% mitten codes up to [[1400,280,≤28]] with circuit-level thresholds above 10^-3 and sub-50 μs stabiliser cycles, two to three orders of magnitude faster than neutral-atom implementations.
summaries.zh: 作者提出NeST，一种基于方形晶格上嵌套传送带式穿梭轨道的硅自旋量子比特架构，用以实现基于非阿贝尔群的量子LDPC码，获得速率20%、最大达[[1400,280,≤28]]的mitten码，其电路级阈值超过10^-3，稳定子周期低于50微秒，比中性原子实现快两到三个数量级。
summaries.ja: 著者らは、正方格子上の入れ子状コンベヤーベルト型シャトリング軌道を用いたシリコンスピン量子ビットアーキテクチャNeSTを提案し、非可換群に基づく量子LDPC符号を実現して、レート20%で最大[[1400,280,≤28]]のmitten符号を得るとともに、回路レベル閾値10^-3超、50マイクロ秒未満のスタビライザー周期を達成し、中性原子実装より2〜3桁高速であることを示した。

title: Structured PARAFAC Channel Estimation for Flexible Intelligent Metasurface Receivers
abstract: Flexible intelligent metasurfaces (FIMs) create geometric diversity through aperture morphing, but their configuration-dependent responses complicate uplink channel estimation. This letter considers multiple users sharing a common angular response and develops a structured PARAFAC model across calibrated FIM configurations. Its known identity factor and rank-one pilot-weighted channel factor enable deterministic, noniterative algebraic factor recovery through per-element rank-one approximations, reference-state normalization, global rank-one projection, and a least-squares morphing-factor update. The recovered spatial and morphing factors are then jointly matched to the calibrated manifold to estimate the common angles, user gains, and configuration-dependent channels. Simulations demonstrate accurate recovery and show that out-of-plane morphing resolves the azimuth-sign ambiguity of an undeformed planar aperture; an angular-spread experiment quantifies the mismatch when the common-response assumption is relaxed.

summaries.en: This letter develops a structured PARAFAC channel estimation method for flexible intelligent metasurface receivers that exploits a known identity factor and rank-one pilot-weighted channel factor to enable deterministic noniterative recovery of spatial and morphing factors for joint angle and gain estimation, with simulations showing that out-of-plane morphing resolves the azimuth-sign ambiguity of an undeformed planar aperture.
summaries.zh: 本文提出了一种面向柔性智能超表面接收机的结构化PARAFAC信道估计方法，利用已知的单位因子和秩一导频加权信道因子实现确定性的非迭代空间与形变因子恢复，从而联合估计角度和增益，仿真表明离面形变可消除未形变平面孔径的方位角符号模糊。
summaries.ja: 本論文は、既知の単位因子とランク1のパイロット重み付きチャネル因子を利用して空間因子とモーフィング因子を決定論的かつ非反復的に復元し、角度と利得を同時推定するフレキシブルインテリジェントメタサーフェス受信機向けの構造化PARAFACチャネル推定法を提案し、シミュレーションにより面外モーフィングが未変形平面開口の方位角符号の曖昧性を解消することを示す。

title: Multi-Threshold Sampling: Local and Global Parameter Identifiability
abstract: Multi-threshold (MT) sampling records threshold-crossing times for parameter estimation in applications including positron emission tomography, oil well logging, and photon-counting X-ray imaging. We study whether the distribution of recorded crossings uniquely determines the signal parameters and how many thresholds are required for this identifiability. For a fixed MT sampler, we show that the ranks of distribution derivatives with respect to the parameters cannot increase through crossing, timing, and selection. Under suitable regularity assumptions, we characterize local identifiability by a full-rank Jacobian of finitely many event probabilities defined on recorded crossings and establish a necessary and sufficient global identifiability criterion under additional rank and topological assumptions. For a nonhomogeneous Poisson signal model with four intensity parameters, a fixed known single-photon response, and deterministic MT sampling, we prove that four cumulative probabilities of the first recorded crossing time establish local and global identifiability under their respective conditions using a single sufficiently small positive threshold. This attains the minimum number of thresholds for the specified model and sampler. Numerical experiments illustrate these results and reveal weak parameter sensitivity and substantial finite-sample estimation errors when estimation uses these probabilities. The results establish parameter uniqueness while highlighting the role of statistical sensitivity in accurate estimation.

summaries.en: The paper analyzes when multi-threshold sampling of threshold-crossing times uniquely identifies signal parameters, showing that a single sufficiently small positive threshold yields local and global identifiability for a four-parameter nonhomogeneous Poisson intensity model with known single-photon response and deterministic sampling, while numerical experiments reveal weak sensitivity and substantial finite-sample estimation errors.
summaries.zh: 该论文分析了多阈值采样中阈值穿越时间何时能唯一确定信号参数，证明了在已知单光子响应和确定性采样的四参数非齐次泊松强度模型下，单个足够小的正阈值即可实现局部和全局可辨识性，同时数值实验揭示了参数敏感性较弱以及有限样本下估计误差较大的问题。
summaries.ja: 本論文は、マルチスレッショルドサンプリングにおける閾値交差時刻が信号パラメータを一意に特定できる条件を解析し、既知の単一光子応答と決定論的サンプリングを用いた4パラメータ非同次ポアソン強度モデルにおいて、十分に小さい単一の正の閾値で局所的および大域的な識別可能性が達成されることを示す一方、数値実験によりパラメータ感度の弱さと有限標本での大きな推定誤差を明らかにした。
